title: Keep-on-Death Gear
needs_owner_check: The killer's 80% share of the death fee is written as a game rule from ChromaBound config.yml (killer-payout: 80); confirm it is fine to show on the wiki.
summary: **Keep-on-Death Gear** is the SMP rule that Chromatic, Halloween and Living Prism gear stays with you when you die.
infobox: Chromatic, Halloween, Living Prism, Shattered gear

blocks.p: Everything else drops as normal, and every death costs a small share of your balance.
When you die, these items are taken out of your drops and handed back when you respawn:

ul: {{icon:chromatic_chestplate}} Every Chromatic item: weapons, tools and armour.
{{icon:living_prism_chestplate}} Living Prism gear: armour, sword, bow, crossbow, tools, spear, mace and wings.
Shattered gear (a broken Chromatic, Halloween or Living Prism item waiting for repair).

blocks.p: Bound gear says **It seems bound to you** in its lore. Living Prism and Prismatic Resin materials are not gear, and they drop. So do old Chromatic armour pieces made before the switch to the current items.
Every death takes a share of your balance. The money is gone, except the part paid to a player who killed you.

ul: Overworld, Nether, End and spawn: 0.5% of your balance.
If a player killed you, they get 80% of your fee. This does not happen at spawn, where the fee is charged but nobody is paid.
Logging out during PvP combat kills you and costs 5% of your balance. Outside spawn, 80% of it goes to your last opponent.
The fee never takes you below $0. Money held in auction house buy orders and unclaimed auction money counts as part of your balance.
Your other items lie where you died. `/back` takes you there, so go straight away.
Stay online until PvP combat ends. A combat log costs ten times a normal death.
Gear that is about to break shatters instead, and you keep it. Repair it at `/craft repair`.
